Level 1: Trivial Baseline.Radial Pair: Create a simple 2-bus radial AC network. Connect Bus 1 to Bus 2 with a single network line. Place a synchronous generator on Bus 1 and a shunt load on Bus 2.

Level 2: Intermediate.Microgrid: Design a 5-bus AC grid. Bus 1 is the slack bus with an infinite bus connection. Buses 2, 3, and 4 form a ring network. Bus 5 is connected radially to Bus 4. Place a Grid-Forming (GFM) inverter on Bus 2, a Grid-Following (GFL) inverter on Bus 4, and battery energy storage (BESS) on Bus 5. Add shunt loads on buses 3 and 5.

Level 3: Advanced.Tuned Inverters: Generate a 3-bus AC system connected sequentially. Bus 1 has a standard synchronous generator. Bus 2 has a PV-GFM inverter, but override its nominal DC link capacitor (C_dc) to 1.5 and its filter resistance (Rf) to 0.02. Bus 3 is just a shunt load. Make the line between Bus 1 and 2 very long by setting its series R to 0.05 and wL to 0.8.

Level 4: Adversarial.Ambiguous/Out-of-Scope: I need a 4-bus power system. Put a load on Bus 4 and a GFL inverter on Bus 2. Make sure the main grid connection is on Bus 1. Also, connect 1 to 2, 2 to 3, and 3 to 4. Leave Bus 3 empty. Finally, add a DC microgrid attached to Bus 4.
